summary: Complete extraction of the 29-page paper proving the hyperbolic Ax–Schanuel conjecture. For a connected pure Shimura variety X = Γ\Ω with uniformization q : Ω → X and graph D ⊂ Ω × X, every irreducible component of W ∩ D of larger than expected dimension, for W ⊂ Ω × X algebraic, projects into a proper weakly special subvariety of X: all atypical intersections are accounted for by the bi-algebraic subvarieties. The proof combines o-minimality — the definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set, the definable Chow and Remmert–Stein theorems of Peterzil and Starchenko, and the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem — with the exponential volume growth of Hwang and To, the Zariski density of monodromy after André and Deligne, and a triple induction. The paper then proves a version with derivatives, for which it develops the Schwarzian differential equation of a Hermitian symmetric domain in jet spaces, showing that the G(ℂ)-translates of q are exactly the solutions of an algebraic differential system; this gives that a basis of modular functions with its partial derivatives to order at least 2 has transcendence degree dim G, generalising Bertrand–Zudilin. Finally it gives a differential-field version and shows that it implies the jet version. Of the 39 items, none is in the pinned libraries, 8 are planned by existing layers, and 31 are missing. The routing follows the atlas's own commitment: LD.6 plans o-minimality and Pila–Wilkie and names Ax–Schanuel among the inputs whose full proofs it must acquire, so the paper becomes a Part II of that roadmap, since Schwarzians, jet spaces, Ochiai's theorem and differential fields are new layers rather than additions to an o-minimality layer; the two definable GAGA theorems go to LD.6 itself, and weakly special subvarieties, which occur nowhere in the atlas, to ShimuraData D4 alongside the other distinguished classes. Five misprints were found and are recorded under sourceIssues; none affects a proof. This is a paper inventory and routing, not a proof blueprint: the results quoted from Peterzil–Starchenko, Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev, Hwang–To, André, Deligne, Ochiai, Mok, Pila–Wilkie, Seidenberg and Kazhdan are recorded as items with their own prerequisite entries and are not decomposed here. Independent review REV-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (Claude Code, cc-442dc5): 44 items (8 planned, 36 missing) and three routes. The ShimuraData D4 source route was rejected and its item moved into the Part II. Five items were added (40–44), with a ComplexComparisonPartII source route for item 40. Items 2, 36 and 38 were corrected, and six further misprints were recorded (E6–E11). Fixes FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b), applying the 13 confirmed findings of RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 against the published version (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978): 49 items (8 planned, 41 missing). Items 4, 5, 13, 14, 16, 18–20, 22, 23, 29–33, 41 and 43 were corrected; items 45–49 were added (the smallest weakly special envelope, the 2-sorted Theorem 1.2 of the published version, Theorem A, the highest-weight tangent orbit and Ochiai's Theorem B) and routed to the Part II; misprints and errors E12–E14 were recorded; the Mok prerequisite and three DOIs were corrected; and the Part II brief now carries the design obligations of the fixes, including the unresolved Lemma 11.1 prerequisite.

items.name: The uniformization of a connected pure Shimura variety and algebraic subvarieties of Ω × X
items.statement: Let Ω be a Hermitian bounded symmetric domain attached to a semisimple group G and Γ ⊂ G(ℤ) a finite-index subgroup, so that X = Γ\Ω is a quasi-projective variety — a connected pure Shimura variety. Let q : Ω → X be the projection and D ⊂ Ω × X the graph of q. The domain Ω sits as an open subset of its compact dual Ω̂, a projective variety; an algebraic subvariety W ⊂ Ω × X means a complex-analytically irreducible component of Ŵ ∩ (Ω × X) for an algebraic Ŵ ⊂ Ω̂ × X.
items.note: The quasi-projectivity of Γ\Ω is Baily–Borel, planned at ShimuraVarieties V2 and V3; the Hermitian domain and its compact dual with the Borel embedding are planned at ShimuraData D2 and D3, and the arithmetic group with its properly discontinuous action at ShimuraVarieties V0 and V1. The bi-algebraic convention for subvarieties of Ω × X — algebraic in the compact dual, restricted to the domain — is the paper's own and is the shape in which every statement below is made.

items.name: Weakly special and special subvarieties
items.statement: The paper does not define weakly special subvarieties; it takes them from Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev [18] (p. 1). What it uses is the following. A connected Shimura variety X carries a collection of weakly special subvarieties; the special subvarieties are the weakly special ones containing a special point, and play no role here. Weakly special subvarieties are bi-algebraic in the sense of [18], so they give rise to atypical intersections: for W = Ω₁ × X₁ with X₁ weakly special and Ω₁ a connected component of its preimage, dim W = dim U + dim X₁ (p. 2). They come in countably many families, which correspond to points of suitable (possibly constructible) subvarieties of countably many Hilbert schemes; these families are defined over Q̄, and the collection of families is stable under Galois automorphisms (§12.1, p. 24; the countability is also used in the proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 9).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §1, pp. 1–2, and §12.1, p. 24; the notion is cited from Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev [18]
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19. The earlier statement said weakly special subvarieties are exactly the bi-algebraic ones. The paper asserts only one direction; the converse is a theorem of Ullmo–Yafaev that it does not use. The countably-many-families property, used in Lemma 4.3 and §12.1, was added. The item is rerouted from ShimuraData D4 to the Part II. D4 comes before the construction of X = Γ\Ω, since ShimuraVarieties V0 depends on D5, which depends on D4. So D4 cannot own subvarieties of X without a dependency cycle. PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 routes the same notion to LD.6; one owner must be chosen when these are designed.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties
items.statement: Let W ⊂ Ω × X be an algebraic subvariety and U an irreducible component of W ∩ D whose dimension is larger than expected, that is codim U < codim W + codim D, equivalently dim W < dim U + dim X. Then the projection of U to X is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.1, p. 2; proved in §4, pp. 7–9
items.note: The hyperbolic Ax–Schanuel conjecture. For q = exp : ℂⁿ → (ℂ^×)ⁿ the statement is an equivalent form of Ax's theorem, although (ℂ^×)ⁿ is a mixed and not a pure Shimura variety and so is not formally covered. Every component of such an intersection has dimension at least dim W − dim X, so the theorem says that all atypical components are accounted for by weakly special subvarieties. It generalises the Ax–Lindemann theorem and is expected to play the role there that Ax–Lindemann plays for André–Oort, with applications to Zilber–Pink; Bakker–Tsimerman generalise it to variations of Hodge structure. Collated by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/9): the published Theorem 1.1 (p. 946) assumes in addition that W = Ŵ ∩ (Ω × X) for one irreducible subvariety Ŵ ⊂ Ω̂ × X, and the published §1 defines an algebraic subvariety of Ω × X as a finite union of irreducible ones; arXiv v3 instead calls an irreducible component of Ŵ ∩ (Ω × X) an algebraic subvariety. The design should state the published form.

items.name: Transcendence degree of modular functions and their derivatives
items.statement: Let z₁, …, z_n be an N⁺(ℂ)-invariant algebraic coordinate system on Ω, where N⁺ ⊂ G is the unipotent radical of a parabolic opposite to the parabolic B defining Ω̂ = G/B, and let φ₁, …, φ_N be finitely many modular functions generating the field of modular functions over ℂ, all defined on a common nonempty open subset of Ω. Then the field generated by the φ_i and their partial derivatives with respect to the z_j up to order k ≥ 2 has transcendence degree dim G over ℂ, and the same over ℂ(z₁, …, z_n).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.2, p. 3; proved as Corollary 9.3, p. 18; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 1.3, p. 948, proved as Corollary 9.3, pp. 965–966
items.note: A generalisation of a result of Bertrand and Zudilin for Siegel modular varieties, with the caveat that their result holds over any algebraically closed subfield of ℂ whereas here there is no control over the field of definition of the differential equations. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/12), propagating the confirmed errata entry E3 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json: both versions say "a ℂ-basis of modular functions", but the modular function field has no finite ℂ-basis (1, f, f², … are independent for nonconstant f); finitely many field generators are meant. The transcendence-degree statements are unchanged; E3 also records that the proof must use the field generated by the φ_j and their derivatives.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel with derivatives, in coordinates
items.statement: Let V ⊂ Ω be an irreducible complex analytic variety not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety, let {z_i} be an algebraic coordinate system on Ω, and let {φ_j^{(ν)}} consist of finitely many modular functions φ₁, …, φ_N generating the field of modular functions over ℂ, all defined at at least one point of V, together with their partial derivatives with respect to the z_j up to order k ≥ 2. Then tr.deg._ℂ ℂ({z_i}, {φ_j^{(ν)}}) ≥ dim G + dim V, all functions being restricted to V.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.3, pp. 3–4; proved as Corollary 10.4, p. 21; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 1.4, p. 949, proved as Corollary 10.4, p. 968
items.note: The jet-space-free consequence of Theorem 9.1, along the lines of the Pila–Tsimerman result for Cartesian powers of the j-function. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/12), propagating the confirmed errata entry E3 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json: both versions say "a ℂ-basis of modular functions", but the modular function field has no finite ℂ-basis (1, f, f², … are independent for nonconstant f); finitely many field generators are meant. The transcendence-degree statements are unchanged; E3 also records that the proof must use the field generated by the φ_j and their derivatives.

items.name: Differential Ax–Schanuel
items.statement: Let G, q and a differential field (K, D, C) with a finite set D of commuting derivations and constant field C be as in §12, and let (z, x, y) be a uniformized locus of rank k. Then tr.deg._C C(z, x, y) ≥ rank(z) + dim G, unless x is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.4, p. 4, and Theorem 12.3, p. 25; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 1.5, and Theorem 12.1, p. 973 (numbered 12.3 in v3)
items.note: The differential-field version, which in turn directly implies the jet version. It rests on the fact that all solutions of the relevant differential system are G-translates of q, which comes from the provenance of the system in the Schwarzian attached to G and Ω.

items.name: o-minimal structures, definable sets and the structure R_an,exp
items.statement: The language of o-minimal structures over a real closed field, definable sets and cell decomposition; throughout the paper 'definable' means definable in the o-minimal structure R_an,exp, whose o-minimality is due to van den Dries and Miller building on Wilkie.
items.note: LD.6 plans exactly this: 'Construct the selected o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition'. LD.0 plans the underlying first-order language and definability framework. Review note: LD.6 plans only 'the selected o-minimal structures'. The o-minimality of R_an,exp (van den Dries–Miller, van den Dries–Macintyre–Marker, building on Wilkie) is covered by that phrase, not named. PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 routes the same o-minimality inputs to LD.6 as a source.

items.name: Definability of the uniformization on a Siegel fundamental set
items.statement: Let F be the classical Siegel domain for the action of Γ on Ω. Then the restriction q|_F of the uniformization to F is definable in R_an,exp. For a general Shimura variety this is due to Klingler, Ullmo and Yafaev, generalising results of Peterzil and Starchenko for moduli spaces of abelian varieties.
items.note: The bridge between the o-minimal and the Shimura-variety sides, without which none of §3 is available. LD.6 names 'definability of uniformization' among the inputs its applications are built from, but does not plan it for Shimura varieties, and neither ShimuraVarieties nor ShimuraData mentions definability; Siegel sets themselves are planned at ShimuraVarieties V0.

items.name: Definable Remmert–Stein
items.statement: Let M be a definable complex manifold and E a definable complex analytic subset of M. If A is a definable complex analytic subset of M − E, then its closure Ā is a complex analytic subset of M.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 2.1, p. 5, quoting Peterzil–Starchenko
items.note: One of the two definable GAGA-type theorems on which the paper's algebraicity results rest. LD.6 plans o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition and is the layer that should own this and the next two items, but its text does not mention them; a search of every stage description for 'Peterzil' and 'definable Chow' returns nothing.

items.name: Definable Chow
items.statement: Let Y be a quasiprojective algebraic variety and A ⊂ Y definable, complex analytic and closed in Y. Then A is algebraic. Consequently, if A ⊂ Y is definable and constructible complex analytic — that is, in the boolean algebra generated by closed complex analytic varieties — then A is constructible algebraic.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.3, p. 5
items.note: A slight strengthening of a theorem of Peterzil and Starchenko, obtained by combining their statement with definable Remmert–Stein; the same strengthening was observed by Scanlon and, in a less general form, by Pila and Tsimerman. The corollary follows by induction on dimension. This is the engine of §3: any Γ-invariant analytic set that is definable on a fundamental domain descends to an algebraic set.

items.name: Algebraicity of descended definable analytic sets
items.statement: Let A ⊂ Ω × X be a closed complex analytic set which is Γ × {id}-invariant and such that A ∩ (F × X) is definable. Then (q × id)(A) ⊂ X × X is a closed algebraic subset; if A is moreover constructible complex analytic, then (q × id)(A) is a constructible algebraic subset.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, p. 6
items.note: The converse to the evident fact that the preimage of an algebraic subvariety is Γ-invariant, closed analytic and definable on a fundamental domain. It is proved in two lines from definable Chow, and it is the crucial new algebraicity observation of the paper.

items.name: Descending Hilbert-scheme loci
items.statement: Fix a smooth projective compactification X̂ of X, an algebraic W ⊂ Ω × X with Zariski closure Ŵ ⊂ Ω̂ × X̂, and U an irreducible component of W ∩ D. Let M be the Hilbert scheme of subvarieties of Ω̂ × X̂ with the Hilbert polynomial of Ŵ, B the universal family, A = {(z,x,y) : (z,x) ∈ W_y ∩ D} and, for each k, A(k) the closed analytic locus where the fibre dimension of θ : A → M at (z,x) is at least k. With ψ : Ω × X × M → Ω × X, put Z = Z(k) = ψ(A(k)). Then Z is closed, Γ-invariant and definable on F × X, so T = (q × id)(Z) ⊂ X × X is closed and algebraic.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §3.1 and Lemma 3.3, pp. 6–7
items.note: The construction that turns the family of atypical intersections into an algebraic family on X × X, so that the monodromy theorem of André and Deligne can be applied to it. The paper notes that Lemma 3.3 can also be proved by the more geometric compactification methods of Mok and Mok–Zhong, using L² estimates for ∂̄.

items.name: The stabilizer of a very general member is finite
items.statement: Inside the proof of Theorem 1.1 by contradiction: let W ⊂ Ω × X be algebraic and U an irreducible component of W ∩ D with dim W < dim U + dim X whose projection to X is not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety, and assume Theorem 1.1 for smaller dim Ω, for smaller dim W − dim U at the same dim Ω, and for larger dim U (the triple induction of §4). Carry out §3.1 with k = dim U; let A(k)′ be the irreducible component of A(k) containing U × [W], F₀ the corresponding family, Γ₀ ⊂ Γ the subgroup stabilizing every member of F₀, and Θ the identity component of the Zariski closure of Γ₀ in G. Then Θ is a normal subgroup of G (Lemma 4.1); and after replacing W by a very general member of F₀ (invariant by exactly Γ₀), Θ is the identity subgroup (Lemma 4.2). These are steps of the contradiction argument, not theorems about arbitrary Hilbert families.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2, pp. 7–8; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, §4, Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2, pp. 953–954
items.note: Normality comes from the Zariski density of the monodromy group of V, via the properness of Γ\A(k)′ → V and stab(γ·W′) = γ stab(W′) γ^{-1}. Triviality is an induction: if Θ were positive-dimensional then G would be isogenous to Θ × Θ′, Ω and X would split accordingly, and the inductive hypothesis on the smaller factor would give dim U + dim X ≤ dim W, contradicting atypicality. Restated by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/8): in the bare §3.1 setting the conclusion fails (W = Ω × X, U = D gives Γ₀ = Γ and Θ = G°). The hypotheses of the counterexample are now part of the statement.

items.name: An atypical component forces an infinite stabilizer
items.statement: Under the hypotheses and constructions of item 13 (inside the contradiction argument for Theorem 1.1, with W a very general member of F₀), W is invariant by an infinite subgroup of Γ (Lemma 4.3). Together with item 13 this is the contradiction that proves Theorem 1.1; it is not an unconditional statement about atypical components.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemma 4.3, pp. 8–9; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Lemma 4.3, pp. 954–955
items.note: The counting argument. The definable set I = {γ ∈ G(ℝ) : dim_ℝ((γ·W) ∩ D ∩ (F × X)) = dim_ℝ U} contains every γ ∈ Γ for which U meets γF × X; the volume of (γ·W) ∩ D ∩ (F × X) is uniformly bounded, by the Siegel-coordinate covering of Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev, while by Hwang–To (item 16) the volume of the positive-dimensional projection of U to Ω inside a hyperbolic ball B(R) ⊂ Ω grows exponentially in R (the printed expression γ·W ∩ X ∩ B(R) is ill-typed; sourceIssue E14), so I contains polynomially many integer matrices. Pila–Wilkie then produces real algebraic curves in I containing at least two integer points, and either W is stabilized by a nontrivial integer point or the induction on dim W − dim U or on dim U can be advanced. Restated by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/8): a point W = {(z, q(z))} at torsion-free level satisfies the §3.1 setting but has trivial stabilizer.

items.name: The Pila–Wilkie counting theorem
items.statement: For a definable set in an o-minimal structure, the number of rational points of height at most T lying outside the algebraic part of the set is O_ε(T^ε); in particular a definable set containing more than polynomially many integer points of bounded height contains a positive-dimensional real algebraic subset.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in Lemma 4.3, p. 9, and Lemma 10.3, p. 21
items.note: LD.6 plans 'a source-complete Pila-Wilkie rational-point estimate outside the algebraic part with explicit height and epsilon quantifiers', and its acceptance condition insists that removing the algebraic part is essential.

items.name: Hwang–To exponential volume growth for analytic subvarieties of a Hermitian symmetric domain
items.statement: Let Ω be a bounded symmetric domain with a G(ℝ)-invariant Kähler metric, and let Z ⊂ Ω be a closed complex analytic subvariety of positive dimension. Then the volume of Z ∩ B(x, R), for B(x, R) the geodesic ball of radius R about a point x ∈ Z, grows at least exponentially in R, with constants depending on Ω, the normalisation of the metric, dim Z and the multiplicity of Z at x as in Hwang–To [14, Th. 2]. It is applied in Lemma 4.3 upstairs, to the positive-dimensional projection of U (equivalently of (γ·W) ∩ D) to Ω, not to a subvariety of the quotient Γ\Ω.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in Lemma 4.3, p. 9; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Lemma 4.3, p. 955; quoting Hwang–To [14, Th. 2]
items.note: The complex-geometric input that, played against the uniform volume bound coming from definability, produces the polynomially many integer points required by Pila–Wilkie. It appears nowhere in the atlas: a search of every stage description for 'Hwang' returns nothing. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/6). The earlier statement put the growth on an algebraic subvariety of a quotient, where it is false: in a finite-area modular curve every ball has area at most the area of the curve, and a point has no positive growth. The exact hypotheses and constants of Hwang–To Theorem 2 have not been read; the primary paper must be acquired and its statement checked before blueprint decomposition. The uniform bound on each fundamental-domain piece (Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev, Lemma 5.8) is a separate input and is kept in item 14.

items.name: Zariski density of monodromy for subvarieties not contained in a weakly special subvariety
items.statement: A subvariety of a Shimura variety which is not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety has Zariski-dense monodromy group.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §4, p. 7, and §10, p. 20, quoting André and Deligne
items.note: The group-theoretic input that makes Lemma 4.1 work. It is not planned: the atlas's monodromy layers are about local systems on curves and about the geometric monodromy of families, not about the Zariski closure of the monodromy of a subvariety of a Shimura variety.

items.name: Jet spaces and maps between them
items.statement: For X a smooth complex algebraic variety and k, g ≥ 1, set D^k_g = Spec ℂ[ε₁,…,ε_g]/M^{k+1} with M = (ε₁,…,ε_g), and define the jet space of order k by J^g_kX := Hom(D^k_g, X). Then J^g_0X = X, J^1_1X is the tangent bundle, J^g_k is a functor with natural projections J^g_k → J^g_r for k > r, and one writes J_kX for J^{dim X}_kX. For a, b ≥ 1 and fixed arity g, the ring map ℂ[ε]/M^{a+b+1} → ℂ[t]/M^{a+1} ⊗ ℂ[s]/M^{b+1}, ε_i ↦ 1 ⊗ s_i + t_i ⊗ 1, induces the truncated addition D^g_a × D^g_b → D^g_{a+b} and hence π_{a,b} : J^g_{a+b}X → J^g_a(J^g_bX), injective on points, with π_{a,b} ∘ J^g_{a+b}f = J^g_a(J^g_bf) ∘ π_{a,b} for f : X → Y. The arity g is the same in both factors; the abbreviation J_k = J^{dim X}_k is not nested (J^1_1(J^1_1A¹) has dimension 4, J^2_1(A²) has dimension 6).
items.note: The setting in which Ax–Schanuel with derivatives is most naturally stated. Jet spaces of algebraic varieties are planned nowhere in the atlas: a search of every stage description for 'jet space' returns nothing. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/11): the published §5.2 keeps the source arity in J^{dim X}_aJ_bX; the truncation powers a + b + 1, a + 1, b + 1 are those of the published text.

items.name: Algebraic differential equations as jet subvarieties
items.statement: A holomorphic φ : ℂ^g → ℂ^g satisfying an algebraic differential equation of order m is recorded by the condition J_mφ ∘ id_m(ℂ^g) ⊂ W for a subvariety W ⊂ J_mℂ^g, where id_m : ℂ^g → J_mℂ^g is the natural section a ↦ (z ↦ a + ε). Replacing the target by any variety X, a differential equation is a subvariety W ⊂ J_mX, with no choice of local coordinates on the image. Differentiating the equation is the relation J^g_a(id_b) ∘ id_a = π_{a,b} ∘ id_{a+b}, with the arity g fixed throughout, which gives Im J^g_{a+b}φ ∘ id_{a+b} ⊂ π_{a,b}^{-1}(J^g_aW).
items.note: The coordinate-free formulation of an algebraic differential equation, worked out in the example φ′ = R(φ) where the relation φ″ = R(φ)R′(φ) is recovered geometrically. Not planned anywhere. Amended by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/11): fixed arity g in the differentiation identity.

items.name: The Hodge decomposition of 𝔤 and the N⁺ coordinates on the compact dual
items.statement: Write Ω = G_ℝ/K with K maximal compact, so that Ω sits inside the flag manifold Ω̂ = G_ℂ/B for a complex parabolic B. The Lie algebra decomposes as 𝔤 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ ⊕ 𝔫⁺, a Hodge structure of weight 0 (types (−1, 1), (0, 0) and (1, −1)), with 𝔟 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ and N^± the corresponding abelian unipotent groups. Fixing o ∈ Ω and an identification ℂⁿ ≅ N⁺ gives coordinates on an open subset of Ω̂ and compatible N⁺-invariant sections id_m : N⁺ → J_mN⁺.
items.note: The Hodge decomposition of the adjoint representation, the Borel embedding of Ω in the flag variety G/B and the parabolic stabilizing the Hodge filtration are planned at ShimuraData D2 and D3; the N⁺-coordinate charts and the compatible jet sections are the paper's own packaging of them. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/1): arXiv v3 §7.1 (p. 11) prints weight 2, but the three types sum to zero and the published §7.1 (p. 958) prints weight 0 (sourceIssue E12). The weight is part of the type of a Hodge structure (Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Structure.lean, HodgeStructureOn), so consumers must use weight 0. The general Hodge API stays as it is; the adjoint construction is imported from ShimuraData D2/D3.

items.name: The Schwarzian differential equation and nondegenerate jets
items.statement: Define the Schwarzian differential equation of order m to be W_m := G · id_m(N⁺) = G · id_m(o) ⊂ J_mΩ̂, the locus of jets of maps of the form z ↦ g·z. Define J^{nd,r}_kY ⊂ J^r_kY to be the locus of infinitesimal maps surjective on tangent spaces, which is nonempty only for r ≥ dim Y. For G = PSL₂, Ω = ℍ and m = 3 this recovers the classical Schwarzian derivative.
items.note: The differential equation satisfied by the uniformization map, and the reason all solutions of the relevant system are G-translates of q. The Schwarzian derivative of a Hermitian symmetric domain appears nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Rigidity of the second-order infinitesimal neighbourhood
items.statement: Let G_Ω be the image of G(ℂ) in Aut(Ω̂), that is, G(ℂ) modulo the kernel of its action on Ω̂ (a finite central subgroup when no simple factor of G acts trivially). The subgroup of B fixing id₁(o) is N⁻ (Lemma 7.1, with B = K_ℂN⁻), and G_Ω acts freely on id₂(o), hence on all of J^{nd}_kΩ̂ for k ≥ 2 (Proposition 7.2); equivalently, the stabilizer in G(ℂ) of a nondegenerate jet of order at least 2 is the action kernel. Consequently, if F : Ω̂ → Ω̂ satisfies J₃F ∘ id₃ ⊂ W₃, then F(z) = gz for some g ∈ G(ℂ) (Corollary 7.3).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemma 7.1, Proposition 7.2 and Corollary 7.3, pp. 12–13; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Lemma 7.1, Proposition 7.2 and Corollary 7.3, p. 959
items.note: The freeness statement is what makes the Schwarzian a faithful invariant of a map up to G, and Corollary 7.3 is the characterisation of G-translates by third-order data that the connection formula converts into Theorem 8.2. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/7). Both versions say that G(ℂ) acts freely, which fails for a non-effective action: −I ∈ SL₂(ℂ) fixes every jet on P¹, and the paper's own example G = Sp₂g has a central kernel. Neatness of Γ does not help, since the kernel belongs to the complex group. In the orbit and expected-dimension computations (Lemma 9.2, Corollary 9.3, Theorems 9.1 and 12.1), dim G means dim G_Ω = dim G − dim(kernel). Replacing G by G_Ω changes neither Ω, nor q, nor the action of Γ through its image; it changes dim G only when the kernel is positive-dimensional, in which case the expected-dimension terms must use dim G_Ω.

items.name: Lower-order rigidity in the ball and in rank at least two
items.statement: If n ≥ 2, Ω = B^n and G(ℂ) = PGL(n+1; ℂ), then a map f satisfying J₂f ∘ id₂ ⊂ W₂ is a G(ℂ)-translate (Theorem 7.4). If Ω is an irreducible bounded symmetric domain of rank at least 2 and G(ℂ) = Aut(Ω̂), then a map satisfying J₁f ∘ id₁ ⊂ W₁ is a G(ℂ)-translate (Theorem 7.5). Both extend to reducible Ω provided no irreducible factor is the disc, respectively provided every irreducible factor has rank at least 2.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorems 7.4 and 7.5, pp. 13–15
items.note: Theorem 7.4 follows from a local holomorphic version of the Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry over ℂ (Theorem A, proved in Mok's book), and Theorem 7.5 from Ochiai's theorem characterising automorphisms of S-structures on an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of compact type of rank at least 2 (Theorem B). They allow the order-3 hypothesis of Corollary 7.3 to be lowered in these cases. Amended by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/13): Theorem 7.4 consumes item 47 (Theorem A) and Theorem 7.5 consumes items 48–49 (the highest-weight tangent orbit and Ochiai's Theorem B).

items.name: The Schwarzian variety, the map ψ_k and the connection formula
items.statement: Define the k-th Schwarzian variety by S_k(Ω̂) := G\J_kΩ̂ ≅ B\J_kΩ̂(o) birationally, and for a rational F : Ω̂ → Ω̂ set S_k(F)(z) = G·J_kF(id_k(z)) ∈ S_k(Ω̂). There is a rational map ψ_k : S_k(Ω̂) × (N⁺\J_k(Ω̂)) → S_k(Ω̂), extended to powers, and for any two maps F₁, F₂ the connection formula ψ_k(S_k(F₁)(F₂(z)), J_kF₂(id_k(z))) = S_k(F₁ ∘ F₂)(z) holds.
items.note: For the upper half plane and k = 3 this is the classical Schwarzian and its classical composition law. The connection formula is the identity that lets the Schwarzian of the inverse uniformization be computed, and hence lets Proposition 8.1 be proved by descent.

items.name: Schwarzians of automorphic functions are algebraic
items.statement: Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete with X = Γ\Ω a Shimura variety, let φ = (φ₁, φ₂) : X → Ω̂² be a rational embedding and p_i = φ_i ∘ q. Then (S_k(p₁^{-1})(φ₁(x)), S_k(p₂^{-1})(φ₂(x))) is an algebraic function R_k(x) of x ∈ X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Proposition 8.1, p. 16
items.note: Proved by observing that the expression is definable on a fundamental domain, by the connection formula and the definability of q|_F, and Γ-invariant, hence algebraic by definable Chow. A rational embedding into Ω̂² always exists because the function field of X is that of an irreducible hypersurface and Ω̂ is rational.

items.name: Characterisation of the uniformization by its Schwarzian
items.statement: Let U ⊂ Ω̂ be a connected open set and F : U → φ(X) ⊂ Ω̂² satisfy ψ₃(R₃(φ^{-1}(F(z))), J₃F(id₃(z))) = (S₃(id), S₃(id)). Then F(z) = p(gz) for some g ∈ G(ℂ).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 8.2, p. 16
items.note: The statement that the algebraic differential equation satisfied by the uniformization has, as its only solutions, the G(ℂ)-translates of it. By Theorems 7.4 and 7.5 one may use R₂ when Ω = B^n with n ≥ 2 and R₁ when Ω is irreducible of rank at least 2.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel with derivatives, in jet spaces
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 and r ≥ dim X be positive integers and let W ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX be an algebraic subvariety. Let U be an irreducible component of W ∩ J^{nd,r}_kD whose dimension is larger than expected, that is dim W < dim U + dim G. Then the projection of U to X is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 9.1, p. 17; proved in §10, pp. 20–21
items.note: The jet-space form of the main theorem, from which Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 follow as Corollaries 9.3 and 10.4. Note that the expected-dimension condition is now governed by dim G rather than dim X, because the graph of the jet prolongation of q has G(ℂ)-orbit of dimension dim G. Collated by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/9): the published Theorem 9.1 (p. 964) assumes W = Ŵ ∩ (J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX) for one irreducible Ŵ ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kΩ̂ × J^{nd,r}_kX.

items.name: The jet graph has algebraic G-orbit and Zariski closure
items.statement: For k ≥ 2, the graph J^{nd,r}_kD ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX of the jet prolongation J^r_kq is such that G(ℂ) · J^{nd,r}_kD is a closed algebraic subvariety and is the Zariski closure of J^{nd,r}_kD (Lemma 9.2); and for the analogue of the Hilbert-scheme locus Z in jet space, T = (q × id)(Z) ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kX × J^{nd,r}_kX is closed and algebraic (Lemma 9.4).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemmas 9.2 and 9.4, pp. 17–19
items.note: The two algebraicity inputs that let the argument of §§3–4 be rerun in jet space; both come from definable Chow through Theorem 8.2, which identifies the G-orbit as the solution set of an algebraic differential equation. Amended by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/7): the orbit G(ℂ) · J^{nd,r}_kD has dimension computed with the effective group G_Ω of item 22.

items.name: The jet-space analogue of the stabilizer argument
items.statement: Inside the proof of Theorem 9.1 by contradiction, under its counterexample hypotheses (W, U with dim W < dim U + dim G, projection of U to X not in a proper weakly special subvariety) and the corresponding induction hypotheses, with Θ defined as in item 13 but for the jet-space family of §9.3 and W replaced by a very general member: Θ is a normal subgroup of G (Lemma 10.1), Θ is the identity subgroup (Lemma 10.2), and W is invariant by an infinite subgroup of Γ (Lemma 10.3); the contradiction proves Theorem 9.1.
items.note: The proofs follow §4, with the volume and counting arguments carried out on the jet spaces; Corollary 10.4 is then Theorem 1.3. Restated by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/8): the jet-space lemmas carry the same contradiction context as items 13–14.

items.name: Finite-order jets determine a global group element
items.statement: For every positive integer k there is m = m(G, q, k) with the following property: if ∆_k is a k-dimensional disc and (w, u) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × Ω̂ is a pair of maps such that at every t there is g_t ∈ G(ℂ) with u(t) = g_t w(t) to order m, then there is a global g ∈ G(ℂ) with u(t) = g w(t).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemma 11.1, p. 22
items.note: The rigidity statement that turns a pointwise, infinitesimal condition into a global one, and hence makes the differential-algebraic characterisation of §11 possible. Proof status (FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19, RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/5): the printed proof of Lemma 11.1 (published p. 969, v3 p. 22) uses that each strict inclusion of jet stabilizers lowers dimension, which is false (confirmed errata E4 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json: a PSp₄ example whose third- and fourth-order stabilizers have orders 2 and 1). The statement is not refuted, but its proof is an unresolved prerequisite until a valid finite-order determination argument is supplied; the Part II design must not treat Lemma 11.1 as proved.

items.name: Characterising the uniformization map by differential equations
items.statement: With m as above and V^k_m the corresponding locus of jets of order m and arity k, a map (w, u) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × X with J^k_m(w, u) ∘ id_m(∆_k) ⊂ V^k_m satisfies u = q ∘ g ∘ w for a global g ∈ G(ℂ) (Theorem 11.2). Enlarging the data to (w, u, v) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × X × J^n_rX with image in V_{k,m} × V_{n,r} and tangent image in the integrable algebraic foliation W_{n,r}, and requiring v to be compatible with u along w — the zero-order part of v equals u and the first-order part satisfies du = v₁ ∘ dw (or, more strongly, v is the r-jet of u along w) — one gets g ∈ G(ℂ) with (w, u, v) = L(w, g, r) (Theorem 11.3, with the compatibility repaired), under the domain and lifting hypotheses of §11.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorems 11.2 and 11.3, pp. 22–24; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorems 11.2 and 11.3, pp. 970–971
items.note: The foliation W_{n,r} is introduced precisely to force the group element to stay constant when w has a stabilizer; its leaves are the loci where g(t) ∈ gN, and the condition that v restrict to u then forces n(t) = id. The constructible algebraicity of V_{n,ℓ} and W_{n,ℓ} comes from Corollary 3.2. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/5 and /11), propagating the confirmed errata entries E4 and E5 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json. The printed Theorem 11.3 assumes only that v restricts to u (zero-order compatibility); w = 2t, u = q(t), v = J_rq(id_r(t)) satisfies that hypothesis but is not of the form L(w, g, r). The first-order compatibility du = v₁ ∘ dw is now part of the statement. The theorem also rests on Lemma 11.1 (item 30), whose proof is an unresolved prerequisite; the local compatibility repair is not a complete global proof. The k-jet wording was replaced by order m, arity k.

items.name: Differential fields, rank and transcendence degree of a point
items.statement: Let (K, D, C) be a differential field with D = {D₁, …, D_d} a finite set of commuting derivations and C the constant field. For an algebraic variety V over C and p ∈ V(K), take an affine open U ∋ p over C, let S be the image of O(U) in K under evaluation at p, and define the transcendence degree of p to be tr.deg._C Frac(S) and the rank of p to be the rank of the matrix (D_i s)_{i,s}. For points p₁, p₂ of two varieties, p₂ is a function of p₁ if rank(p₁, p₂) = rank(p₁): at regular points this says that p₂ depends locally analytically on p₁, not necessarily rationally over C.
items.note: The differential-algebra vocabulary in which Theorem 1.4 is stated. A search of every stage description in the atlas for 'differential field' and 'differential algebra' returns nothing in this sense. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/3), propagating the confirmed errata entry E7 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json (not the embedded sourceIssue E7 of this file, which is a different misprint). Both versions print rank(p₁, p₂) = rank(p₂), which fails for p₁ = (t, s), p₂ = t and accepts p₁ = t, p₂ = (t, s). The applications in §§12.3 and 12.5 assume equal ranks, where the two tests coincide.

items.name: Uniformized loci of rank k in a differential field
items.statement: Fix a finite-type field of definition L₀ ⊂ ℂ for X and for the differential system satisfied by q, and a finite-type L ⊂ ℂ defining the constructible varieties of §11; assume C contains subfields Λ₀, Λ isomorphic to L₀, L under ι₀, ι. A K-point (z, x, y) of Ω̂ × X × J^n_rX with r ≥ 2, with x and z of the same rank k ≥ 1 and x a function of z, satisfying the differential conditions of Theorem 11.3 including the first-order compatibility of y with x along z (item 31), is a uniformized locus of rank k; under a Seidenberg embedding over ι it becomes an honest tuple of regular functions on a k-dimensional disc.
items.note: The weakly special families come in countably many families defined over ℚ̄ and stable under Galois, so they may be taken to be defined over L₀, which is what makes 'x is contained in a weakly special subvariety' a condition on a K-point. Amended by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/5): the uniformized-locus conditions carry the first-order compatibility of errata E5 (research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json), and Theorem 11.3 inherits the unresolved Lemma 11.1 prerequisite (errata E4).

items.name: Seidenberg's embedding theorem
items.statement: Any finitely generated differential field extension of ℚ embeds into a field of meromorphic functions on some domain, compatibly with a given embedding of the constants.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §12.3, pp. 24–25, in the version given by Scanlon
items.note: The device that converts a differential-algebraic statement into a statement about actual holomorphic functions on a disc, where Theorem 9.1 applies. It appears nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Conjugates of arithmetic varieties are arithmetic
items.statement: A conjugate of an arithmetic variety is again arithmetic.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §12.1, p. 24, quoting Kazhdan, see also Milne
items.note: Quoted as a deep theorem, and needed to ensure that the differential fields considered are identified correctly with the complex objects. It is not planned; ShimuraVarieties V7 plans Milne's conjugation and descent theory for Shimura varieties, which is adjacent but is a statement about canonical models rather than about arithmeticity of conjugates.

items.name: Complex analytic subspaces and Chow's theorem
items.statement: Closed complex analytic subspaces of complex manifolds and of analytifications of algebraic varieties, and Chow's theorem that a closed analytic subset of projective space is algebraic (used in the proof of Theorem 2.2 and throughout §3).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §2 and §3, pp. 5–6
items.note: ComplexComparisonPartII C0 treats closed analytic subspaces with their ideal sheaves, and C4 plans Chow algebraization. Corrected by the review. The earlier statement also claimed the classical Remmert–Stein theorem and the local dimension theory of analytic sets as planned. No layer plans them, and the paper uses only the definable Remmert–Stein theorem (item 9). The analytic inputs the paper does use are now item 40, routed as a source to ComplexComparisonPartII. C2, projective coherent GAGA, is not what this item needs.

items.name: Hilbert schemes of a projective variety
items.statement: The Hilbert scheme parametrising closed subschemes of a projective variety with a fixed Hilbert polynomial, with its universal family and its projectivity.
items.note: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2 plans the Hilbert and Quot functors and R09.1 the projective parameter spaces. The compactness of M is what makes ψ proper and Z closed.

items.name: Arithmetic groups, Siegel sets and fundamental domains
items.statement: Arithmetic subgroups of a semisimple group acting on a Hermitian symmetric domain, reduction theory, Siegel sets and the existence of a fundamental set with finitely many translates covering the quotient.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §2.2 and §4, pp. 5 and 8–9
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 (reduction theory) constructs Siegel sets and proves that finitely many of them cover the arithmetic quotient. ShimuraVarieties V0 consumes that reduction theory for Hermitian domains. Corrected by the review: the earlier citation of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0 (symmetric spaces and components) does not plan Siegel sets.

items.name: The Baily–Borel algebraic structure on an arithmetic quotient
items.statement: An arithmetic quotient Γ\Ω of a Hermitian symmetric domain is a quasi-projective algebraic variety, with a minimal compactification.
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V2 plans Baily–Borel algebraicity and the minimal compactification and V3 Borel algebraicity and uniqueness; V1 plans the analytic tower.

items.name: Proper mapping theorem and semicontinuity of fibre dimension
items.statement: For a holomorphic map of complex analytic spaces, the locus where the local fibre dimension is at least k is a closed analytic subset (Cartan–Remmert semicontinuity), and the image of a closed analytic set under a proper holomorphic map is a closed analytic set (Remmert's proper mapping theorem). The paper uses the first to see that A(k) is closed and complex analytic (§3.1 and §9.2, citing the proof of Peterzil–Starchenko [28, Lemma 8.2]), and the second in the proof of Lemma 9.2 (p. 17).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §3.1, p. 6; §9.2, p. 19; proof of Lemma 9.2, p. 17
items.note: Added by the review. No layer plans these classical theorems of complex analytic geometry. ComplexComparisonPartII C0 builds coherent analytic sheaves and closed analytic subspaces, and C4 uses a proper-projection argument in Chow algebraization, so that roadmap is their owner. PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 routes its proper holomorphic image theorem to the same layers.

items.name: Weighted projective compactification of jet spaces
items.statement: Let Y be a complex manifold and let G_{m,ℂ} act on Hom(D^r_k, Y) × A¹_ℂ by λ · (t ↦ f(t), s) := (t ↦ f(λt), λs). Let Z ⊂ Hom(D^r_k, Y) × A¹_ℂ be the closed locus of pairs (f, 0) with f a constant jet. Set BJ^r_kY := ((Hom(D^r_k, Y) × A¹_ℂ) ∖ Z)/G_{m,ℂ}, equivalently the relative weighted Proj over Y of the graded algebra in which the Taylor coefficients of order |ν| have weight |ν| and s has weight 1. In Taylor-coefficient coordinates it is a bundle of weighted projective spaces over Y, hence projective when Y is projective. The open chart s ≠ 0 is identified with J^r_kY by (f, s) ↦ (t ↦ f(t/s)), so BJ^r_kY compactifies J^r_kY, and for Y quasi-projective with a nonsingular projective compactification Ŷ ⊃ Y, BJ^r_kŶ ⊃ J^r_kŶ ⊃ J^r_kY is a projective compactification. Functoriality: a morphism φ : Y → Y′ induces a morphism BJ^r_kY → BJ^r_kY′ when J^r_kφ sends nonconstant jets to nonconstant jets, in particular for immersions, open embeddings and automorphisms (which is all the paper uses: the action of G(ℂ) on Ω̂ and the open embedding of Y in Ŷ); for an arbitrary morphism it induces only a rational map, defined off the jets it makes constant.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §9.1, p. 19 (announced in footnote 4, p. 17); published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, §9.2, p. 966 (footnote 6, p. 965)
items.note: Added by the review. It is needed for the jet-space Hilbert-scheme construction behind Lemma 9.4 and the proof of Theorem 9.1. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/2). Both versions print the quotient of the whole of Hom(D^r_k, Y) × A¹ and call it a weighted projective space and a functorial compactification. For k = r = 1 over a point of a curve the fibre is A² with weights (1, 1): the origin is an extra orbit in the closure of every other, and only the punctured quotient is P¹. A constant map Y → Y′ sends every boundary point (nonconstant jet, s = 0) to the excluded locus, so it induces no morphism. The statement now removes Z and restricts the functoriality claim (sourceIssue E13). Gluing of the local weighted-projective charts is a design obligation.

items.name: Differential Ax–Schanuel for products (Theorem 12.5)
items.statement: Let z = (z^(1), …, z^(ℓ)) ∈ Ω̂^ℓ(K) with rank(z^(k)) = n for each k, and x = (x^(1), …, x^(ℓ)) ∈ X^ℓ(K), each of rank n, such that x^(i) is a function of z^(i) for each i. Let y^(i) be the partial derivatives of x^(i) with respect to z^(i) up to order r ≥ 2, and put y = (y^(1), …, y^(ℓ)). Suppose (z^(k), x^(k)) ∈ V^k_m for each k. Then tr.deg._C C(z, x, y) ≥ rank(z) + ℓ·dim G, unless x is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X^ℓ. Here the y^(i) are uniquely determined, by linear algebra in the derivatives of z and x.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §12.5, Theorem 12.5, p. 27; published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 12.2, p. 975 (numbered 12.5 in v3)
items.note: Added by the review: a stated theorem, the analogue for q^ℓ : Ω^ℓ → X^ℓ of the exponential and modular cases. The paper gives no separate proof; it is presented as a special case of Theorem 12.3.

items.name: Jet Ax–Schanuel from differential Ax–Schanuel
items.statement: Theorem 12.3 (published Theorem 12.1) implies Theorem 9.1, with two repairs to the printed deduction. Let U ⊂ J^{nd,n}_ℓD (ℓ ≥ 2) be a locus of dimension k on which x is the image of the jet z. (i) The jet coordinates of x generate the same field as the partial derivatives q_i^{(ν)}∘z, |ν| ≤ ℓ: writing the input jet as (z, r, s, …) with r invertible and the output first-order part as R, one has R = (Dq)(z)·r, so Dq = R r⁻¹, and at order j one subtracts the lower-order chain-rule terms and inverts the induced action of r on Sym^j; no local inverse of z is used. (ii) Differential Ax–Schanuel is applied with rank(z) = dim(z), the dimension of the locus parametrized by z, giving dim Zcl(z, x, y, …) ≥ dim(z) + dim G unless the projection of U to X lies in a proper weakly special subvariety; the inequality dim Zcl(A, B) − dim Zcl(A) ≥ dim(A, B) − dim A then supplies the remaining dim U − dim(z).
items.note: Added by the review: the paper's second proof of Theorem 9.1, following Pila–Tsimerman [32]. Corrected by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/4), propagating the confirmed errata entry E6 of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json. The printed deduction claims a map φ with (z, r, s, …)∘φ = id and that (z, x, y) has rank k = rank(z) = dim U; for an unramified modular-curve q and input second jets (a, b, 0) with b ≠ 0, dim U = 2 while rank(z) = 1. The repaired deduction is conditional on Theorem 12.1; it does not prove that input.

items.name: Second-order partial derivatives of q generate all of them
items.statement: For k ≥ 2 the projection J_{k+1}q(G·J^{nd,n}_{k+1}(id_{k+1}(o))) → J_kq(G·J^{nd,n}_k(id_k(o))) is bijective. J_kq(G·J^{nd,n}_k(id_k(o))) is the Zariski closure of the graph of the partial derivatives of q of order |ν| ≤ k. Consequently, for k ≥ 2 the k-th partial derivatives of q are rational in those of order ≤ 2, so the field generated by all partial derivatives of q is generated by those of order ≤ 2.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Remark after Corollary 9.3, p. 18
items.note: Added by the review: a stated consequence of Lemma 9.2 and Proposition 7.2, proved by the argument of Corollary 9.3.

items.name: The smallest weakly special subvariety containing a subset
items.statement: For a subset Y of Ω (or of X), Y^WS denotes the smallest weakly special subvariety of Ω (respectively X) containing Y: the intersection of all weakly special subvarieties containing Y, which is again weakly special (an irreducible component of an intersection of weakly special subvarieties is weakly special).
items.locator: published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 1.2, p. 947 (not in arXiv v3)
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/9). The paper uses the notion without proof; the stability of weakly special subvarieties under intersection is part of their theory after Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev [18] and must be supplied with item 2, which this item extends.

items.name: The 2-sorted Ax–Schanuel inequality
items.statement: Let X, Ω be as in Theorem 1.1 and Y ⊂ Ω an irreducible complex-analytic subset, with Y^WS ⊂ Ω the smallest weakly special subvariety containing Y (item 45). Then dim Y^zar + dim q(Y)^zar ≥ dim Y + dim Y^WS, where Y^zar and q(Y)^zar are the Zariski closures of Y and q(Y).
items.locator: published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, Theorem 1.2, p. 947 (not in arXiv v3)

items.name: The local holomorphic Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry (Theorem A)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2, Ω = Bⁿ, G(ℂ) = PGL(n + 1; ℂ), with the standard embeddings Bⁿ ⋐ ℂⁿ ⊂ Pⁿ. Let U ⊂ ℂⁿ be a convex open set and f : U → V a biholomorphism onto an open subset V ⊂ Pⁿ such that, for every nonempty intersection ℓ ∩ U of an affine line ℓ with U, f(ℓ ∩ U) ⊂ ℓ′ for some affine line ℓ′. Then f extends to a biholomorphic automorphism F : Pⁿ → Pⁿ, i.e. F ∈ PGL(n + 1; ℂ).
items.locator: published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, §7.3, Theorem A, p. 960; arXiv:1711.02189v3, §7.3, pp. 13–14; proved in Mok [23, §(2.3)]
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/13). An external supplier, quoted without proof; it gives Theorem 7.4 (item 23). Its proof is in Mok's 1999 article (prerequisites), which has not been audited here.

items.name: The highest-weight orbit in the projectivised tangent space of a compact Hermitian symmetric space
items.statement: Let S = G/B be an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of the compact type (G simple complex, B maximal parabolic). For x ∈ S let B_x = U · L be a Levi decomposition of the isotropy group. Since dυ(x) = id on T_x(S) for υ ∈ U, γ ↦ dγ(x) is a representation of L = B_x/U on T_x(S), independent of the Levi decomposition; W_x ⊂ PT_x(S) is the highest-weight orbit of L. It coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents C_x(S) at x.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/13). The printed paragraph writes T_x(X) for T_x(S) (sourceIssue E3 of this file).

items.name: Ochiai's theorem (Theorem B)
items.statement: Let S be an irreducible compact Hermitian symmetric manifold of rank at least 2, let U, V ⊂ S be connected open subsets and f : U → V a biholomorphism such that for every x ∈ U the differential df(x) carries W_x onto W_{f(x)} (item 48). Then there is F ∈ Aut(S) with F|_U = f.
items.locator: published Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978, §7.3, Theorem B, p. 960; arXiv:1711.02189v3, §7.3, p. 14; Ochiai [26]
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19/13). An external supplier, quoted without proof; it gives Theorem 7.5 (item 23).

routes.title: Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration, Part II: functional transcendence and Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties
routes.brief: Extend the roadmap Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration in the direction its o-minimality layer LD.6 already points: functional transcendence for the uniformization of a Shimura variety, following Mok, Pila and Tsimerman, Annals of Mathematics 189 (2019). LD.6 plans o-minimal structures, cell decomposition, the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem and Pila–Zannier applications, and names 'independent Galois-orbit and Ax-Lindemann/Ax-Schanuel inputs' among the primary proofs it must acquire; this Part II supplies those inputs, which need layers of their own because their proofs are not model theory but complex geometry, the group theory of Hermitian symmetric domains, and differential algebra. The final theorems are these. (1) Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties (Theorem 1.1): for X = Γ\Ω a connected pure Shimura variety with uniformization q : Ω → X and graph D ⊂ Ω × X, if W ⊂ Ω × X is algebraic and U is an irreducible component of W ∩ D with dim W < dim U + dim X, then the projection of U to X lies in a proper weakly special subvariety. (2) Ax–Schanuel with derivatives (Theorem 9.1): the same statement in the jet spaces J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX with the expected-dimension condition governed by dim G, and its two corollaries — that finitely many generators of the modular function field together with their partial derivatives to order k ≥ 2 has transcendence degree dim G over ℂ and over ℂ(z), and that restricted to a variety V not inside a proper weakly special subvariety the transcendence degree is at least dim G + dim V. (3) Differential Ax–Schanuel (Theorem 12.3): for a differential field (K, D, C) and a uniformized locus (z, x, y) of rank k, tr.deg._C C(z, x, y) ≥ rank(z) + dim G unless x lies in a proper weakly special subvariety. Cover, in layers: weakly special subvarieties of a connected Shimura variety (after Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev), their bi-algebraicity and their countably many families defined over Q̄ (built on the subdata and special points of ShimuraData D4 and the quotients of ShimuraVarieties V0–V3); the definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set, after Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev and Peterzil–Starchenko, and the algebraicity principle it yields — a Γ-invariant closed analytic set definable on a fundamental domain descends to an algebraic subset of X × X; the Hilbert-scheme family of atypical intersections and its descent; the stabilizer argument, with the Zariski density of monodromy after André and Deligne, the exponential volume growth of Hwang–To for positive-dimensional analytic subvarieties of Ω (applied upstairs, to the projection of U to Ω), the uniform volume bound coming from definability, and the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem, assembled into the triple induction on dim Ω, on dim W − dim U and on dim U; jet spaces of algebraic varieties with the maps π_{a,b}, and algebraic differential equations as jet subvarieties together with the geometric form of differentiating an equation; the weight-0 Hodge decomposition 𝔤 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ ⊕ 𝔫⁺, the N⁺-coordinates on the compact dual, and the Schwarzian differential equation W_m = G · id_m(o) with the nondegenerate jet loci; the rigidity results — B fixes id₁(o) exactly on N⁻, the effective image G_Ω of G in Aut(Ω̂) acts freely on id₂(o), a map with J₃ in W₃ is a G(ℂ)-translate, and the lower-order versions in the ball via the Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry and in rank at least 2 via Ochiai's theorem; the Schwarzian variety, the map ψ_k, the connection formula, the algebraicity of the Schwarzian of an automorphic function, and the resulting characterisation of q up to G(ℂ); the jet-space forms of all of the above; and finally the differential-field package — rank and transcendence degree of a K-point, the foliation that keeps the group element constant, uniformized loci, and the Seidenberg embedding that turns a differential-algebraic hypothesis into holomorphic functions on a disc. Every definition gets its API and unit tests, and the two quoted external theorems that are not proved here, Hwang–To volume growth and Kazhdan's theorem that a conjugate of an arithmetic variety is arithmetic, are recorded with their hypotheses. Import, never re-plan: o-minimal structures, definable sets, cell decomposition and the Pila–Wilkie theorem from LD.6 and LD.0, together with the definable Remmert–Stein and definable Chow theorems that this extraction routes to LD.6; Hermitian symmetric domains, the compact dual, the Borel embedding and the Hodge decomposition of the adjoint representation from ShimuraData D2 and D3, and the Shimura data, subdata and special points from D4; arithmetic groups from ShimuraVarieties V0, and Siegel sets and the finite covering of the quotient by them from AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3; the analytic tower and Baily–Borel algebraicity from ShimuraVarieties V1, V2 and V3; closed analytic subspaces, Chow's theorem, Remmert's proper mapping theorem and the semicontinuity of fibre dimension from ComplexComparisonPartII C0 and C4 (the last two through the source route proposed alongside); and Hilbert schemes from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1 and R09.2. Record as downstream, not as targets here, the applications to Zilber–Pink and André–Oort that LD.6 owns. Also cover: the weighted-projective compactification of jet spaces (§9.1) used for jet-space Hilbert schemes; the product version Theorem 12.5; the deduction of Theorem 9.1 from Theorem 12.3 (§12.4); and the remark that the partial derivatives of q of order at most 2 generate all of them. Design constraint added by the review: import only LD.6's o-minimality, cell decomposition and Pila–Wilkie content. LD.6's unlikely-intersection applications consume this Part II, so importing LD.6 as a whole would close a stage cycle. If LD.6 cannot be imported in part, the design job should ask for LD.6 to be narrowed into its counting and application halves. Coordination: PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 routes 'special and weakly special subvarieties' to LD.6. Weakly special subvarieties should have one owner, and this Part II, which already imports ShimuraData and ShimuraVarieties, is the natural one. Fixes by FIX-RT-PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19, all binding on the design. (a) The published version (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 945–978) is now the reference: its Theorem 1.2 is the 2-sorted inequality dim Y^zar + dim q(Y)^zar ≥ dim Y + dim Y^WS (items 45–46, with the smallest weakly special envelope built on item 2); arXiv v3 Theorems 1.2–1.4 are published 1.3–1.5, v3 12.3 and 12.5 are published 12.1 and 12.2, and published Theorems 1.1 and 9.1 add that W is the full restriction of one irreducible Ŵ. (b) The adjoint Hodge structure has weight 0 (item 20). (c) Freeness and the expected-dimension terms use the effective group G_Ω, and dim G means dim G_Ω (item 22). (d) The stabilizer lemmas are steps of the contradiction argument under its hypotheses (items 13, 14, 29). (e) The jet compactification removes the locus (constant jet, s = 0) and is functorial only for maps preserving nonconstant jets (item 41). (f) Jet maps keep the arity fixed (items 18, 19, 31). (g) Lemma 11.1's printed proof is invalid (errata E4): its finite-order determination is an unresolved prerequisite; Theorem 11.3 needs the first-order compatibility du = v₁ ∘ dw (errata E5), and uniformized loci carry it (item 33). (h) The deduction of Theorem 9.1 from Theorem 12.1 recovers derivatives algebraically from the formal matrix r and applies Theorem 12.1 with rank(z) = dim(z) (errata E6, item 43). (i) "p₂ is a function of p₁" means rank(p₁, p₂) = rank(p₁) (errata E7, item 32). (j) Theorems A and B are external supplier items (47–49), citing Mok's 1999 article and Ochiai; their proofs are not decomposed here. The errata entries cited are those of research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19.json.
routes.reason: LD.6 is the layer this paper serves, and it says so itself: its construct-and-export text builds Pila–Zannier applications 'from separate Galois-orbit bounds, definability of uniformization and functional-transcendence theorems', and its source route lists 'independent Galois-orbit and Ax-Lindemann/Ax-Schanuel inputs. Record the exact full proof for each.' So the atlas already commits to acquiring this proof, and the question is only where it goes. It cannot go inside LD.6: that layer is about o-minimal structures, definable sets, cell decomposition and rational-point counting, whereas the bulk of this paper is complex geometry and group theory — the Schwarzian differential equation of a Hermitian symmetric domain, jet spaces, Ochiai's theorem, Hwang–To volume growth, the André–Deligne monodromy theorem — and differential algebra. Those are new layers in LD.6's direction, which is what PROTOCOL.md section 15 calls a Part II. A new roadmap was rejected because the whole point of the theorem is to feed the unlikely-intersection programme LD.6 owns, and because the o-minimal half of the proof is exactly LD.6's subject; a source route was rejected because none of the layers of the parent roadmap plans jets, Schwarzians or differential fields. The parent is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so either route was formally available. Review: accepted, with item 2 (weakly special subvarieties) moved here from the rejected ShimuraData D4 source route and four items added (41–44).

Definable Remmert–Stein and definable Chow, in the form used here, are theorems of o-minimality with no Shimura content: a definable complex analytic subset of a quasiprojective variety, closed in it, is algebraic, and the constructible version follows by induction on dimension. LD.6 plans 'the selected o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition' and is the layer that should own them, but its text does not mention them and a search of every stage description in the atlas for 'Peterzil' and 'definable Chow' returns nothing. They are routed here rather than into the Part II proposed alongside because every consumer of o-minimality in the atlas will want them, not only the functional-transcendence layers: they are the definable form of GAGA. This is a source route on an existing layer of the same roadmap whose Part II takes the rest of the paper, and the two are complementary — the source adds to a layer that exists, the Part II adds layers that do not. Review: accepted. PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 routes overlapping o-minimal inputs to LD.0 and LD.6 as a source; the two source routes are compatible.

Added by the review. The closedness of the fibre-dimension loci A(k) (Cartan–Remmert semicontinuity) and Remmert's proper mapping theorem are classical complex analytic geometry that no layer plans. C0 constructs coherent analytic sheaves and closed analytic subspaces, and C4's Chow algebraization already relies on a proper-projection argument, so the paper is a source for these two layers. PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 routes its proper holomorphic image theorem to the same layers.

sourceIssues.reason: N⁺ acts on the compact dual Ω̂ = G/B, not on X = Γ\Ω, so ν ↦ ν·o makes sense only for o in the domain. Any o ∈ Ω works, since the N⁺-orbit of such a point is open and dense in Ω̂.

sourceIssues.correction: Remove the closed locus of pairs (f, 0) with f a constant jet before taking the quotient (equivalently, take the relative weighted Proj). The result is a bundle of weighted projective spaces over Y containing J^r_kY as the chart s ≠ 0. Functoriality holds for maps that send nonconstant jets to nonconstant jets (immersions, open embeddings, automorphisms); an arbitrary morphism induces only a rational map.
sourceIssues.reason: Over a point of a curve with k = r = 1 the fibre of the printed quotient is A²/G_m with weights (1, 1): the origin is an orbit in the closure of every other orbit, so the orbit space is not P¹, which is the quotient of A² minus the origin.
